title: Non-manipulable domains for the Borda count
summary_en: The Borda count voting rule scores candidates by how voters rank them — but is it manipulable? Barbie, Puppe and Tasnádi characterise the preference domains over which the Borda count is non-manipulable, i.e., on which strategic misreporting cannot improve a voter's outcome. They identify the domain restrictions that immunise Borda from individual manipulation and show how restrictive these conditions are relative to the standard universal-domain framework.
data_used: Theoretical paper in social choice. No primary dataset; results are formal characterisation theorems.
policy_relevance: Theoretical input to the design of voting and committee-decision rules in EU and Hungarian institutions (parliamentary committee voting, public-procurement scoring panels, Eurovision-style ranking aggregations). Practical implication: Borda-count style scoring is robust only on restricted preference domains — a relevant caveat for procurement scoring committees that aggregate evaluator rankings.
